text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PAGER: routing-policy-alert — EU-west p95 latency for economy tier > 800ms over last 3m. Error rate for economy increased (502s) ~4x. Impacting a subset of hosted customers. Paging oncall.

maria: on it. seeing spike in euro nodes, looks correlated with a backend cache flapping around 10:23. any quick mitigations we can push to reduce customer impact?

sam: can we nudge traffic away from economy slab in eu-west to latency-priority lanes? prefer not to change global weights, just region-level steering.

devin: yep — we have a regional gradient policy. I can set economy weight to 0.2 in eu-west and bump lat-priority to soak. doing a quick dry-run to simulate.

kira: heads-up — if we move too much to latency-priority we might blow cost SLO for some accounts on free tier. need to gate it to only affected orgs.

maria: prioritize customer-facing SLA first. can we apply steering only for requests tagged with org != free-tier? we can use the route selector by customer_tier.

elaine: Support here — we already have open tickets from AcmeAnalytics and ShopCart complaining about degraded completion latency. both are on paid plans. this change should help them.

sam: sounds good. plan: 1) regional-weight tweak for economy in eu-west 2) apply a customer_tier selector to avoid forcing free-tier customers onto expensive lanes 3) monitor p95 and 502s for 10m, rollback if errors rise.

devin: executing commands now:
```bash
# set eu-west economy weight and pin selector to paid tiers only
redwood-routingctl set-weight --region eu-west --tier economy --weight 0.2 --selector "customer_tier:paid"
# bump latency-priority weight in the same selector
redwood-routingctl set-weight --region eu-west --tier latency-priority --weight 0.7 --selector "customer_tier:paid"
```

pagerbot: command accepted — change propagated to edge plane (canary -> 30% -> 100%). will report canary metrics in 60s.

maria: while canary rolls, please also throttle request spikes at the ingress to avoid backend queueing. set per-org burst limit for top offenders to 5r/s.

sam: applying quick quota patch for the offenders:
```json
{
  "orgs": ["AcmeAnalytics", "ShopCart"],
  "burst_limit": "5r/s",
  "duration": "10m",
  "reason": "mitigate backend overload during routing adjustment"
}
```

kira: noted — tagging this as non-default gating. Ops, please ensure billing won't be impacted by this internal throttle config.

devin: canary looks good: p95 for affected canary hosts dropped from 850ms -> 310ms, 502s down 70%. rolling to 100% now.

pagerbot: :white_check_mark: rollout success — eu-west economy weight now 0.2 for paid selector. monitoring continues.

maria: awesome — Elaine, can you confirm customer-facing comms? say we reduced latency via temporary routing adjustment and will follow up.

elaine: posting in #support with current mitigation notes and ETA for next update (30m). linking to ticket ids for AcmeAnalytics and ShopCart.

sam: follow-up ops: 1) create a short-lived canary alert for regional routing regressions, 2) add a temporary rule to prevent economy slab from consuming > 40% of eu-west capacity while recovery completes.

devin: created an ephemeral policy:
```yaml
policy_name: eu-west-economy-dampener
scope: region:eu-west, selector: customer_tier:paid
conditions:
  - metric: economy_capacity_utilization
    operator: ">"
    value: 0.4
actions:
  - set_weight: {tier: economy, weight: 0.15}
  - notify: #eng-oncall
ttl: 30m
```

kira: will run a quick cost estimate for the re-route impact and post in thread. rough calc: moving 25% of eu-west economy to latency-priority for 30m ~ +$1200. fine for incident window.

maria: good. assign postmortem owner — sam, can you take? we need root cause, why backend cache flapped, and a runbook action to avoid manual steering next time. also include customer impact summary and billing note.

sam: taking postmortem. I'll open a doc and link it here. expected template: timeline, mitigation steps, RCA, follow-ups (code + playbook).

pagerbot: :page_facing_up: incident ticket created: INC-239876 (owner sam). severity: Sev2. auto-snippets from canary and final metrics attached.

elaine: updating customers now. will note the temporary steering and that normal routing will be restored after stability checks.

devin: monitoring for the next 30m. if p95 creeps above 500ms again, we should consider increasing dedicated pool capacity for eu-west or enable a KV cache warmup.

maria: thanks team. handoff to sam for postmortem and to devin for follow-up infra actions. I'll remain as incident lead until stable. ping me if anything regresses. :pray:
